sections.heading: Is PU Prime Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
PU Prime has grown aggressively since rebranding from Pacific Union, building a 1,000+ instrument catalogue across forex, commodities, indices, shares, ETFs, bonds, and crypto CFDs. The ECN account genuinely delivers institutional-grade pricing — 0.0 pips plus $2 round-turn commission is cheaper than most brokers at any tier. The ASIC licence (410681) is legitimate and active. And a Trustpilot rating of 4.5/5 from over 1,000 reviews suggests the majority of active traders have a positive experience.

But the warning stack is impossible to ignore. The UK FCA warned against Pacific Union (Seychelles) Limited in January 2026 for operating without authorisation. The Danish FSA issued its own warning. Saskatchewan's FCAA published an investor alert in May 2026. And FinTelegram — an independent financial intelligence platform — placed PU Prime on their Red Compliance List. None of these warnings relate to the ASIC-regulated Australian entity. They all target the Seychelles offshore entity that serves the vast majority of PU Prime's global client base.

If you are Australian and trading under ASIC, you have a regulated product with standard protections. If you are anywhere else in the world, you are trading on an entity that four separate regulatory bodies have formally warned against or flagged. That context matters more than any spread number.

sections.heading: Is PU Prime Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — PU Prime holds multiple licences across different jurisdictions. The headline licence is ASIC (Australian Securities and Investments Commission) number 410681, held by PU Prime Trading Pty Ltd. This is a Tier-1 regulator with genuine enforcement power, client money segregation requirements, and negative balance protection for retail clients. Australian residents trading under this entity have meaningful regulatory protection.

The FSCA licence (FSP 52218) covers South African operations. The CMA licence (20200000388) was granted in February 2026 for PU Prime Financial Services LLC operating in the UAE. And the FSC Mauritius licence (GB23202672) provides an additional mid-tier regulatory layer.

But here is the critical distinction: the entity that serves most global retail clients is Pacific Union (Seychelles) Limited, operating under FSA Seychelles licence SD050. This is the entity the UK FCA has specifically warned against. This is the entity the Danish FSA has flagged. And this is the entity that offers 1:1000 leverage with no investor compensation scheme.

Important CySEC clarification: Pacific Union Group Ltd, which held a CySEC licence, has explicitly stated it is NOT part of the PU Prime scheme. Kraken acquired this CySEC entity separately and renamed it Greenfields Wealth. PU Prime does not hold and has never held a CySEC licence.

NAFT last reviewed PU Prime regulation in May 2026.

sections.body:

Not accepted: United States, United Kingdom (FCA warning — do not open an account), Singapore, China, and some EU countries.

sections.practical_note: PU Prime's primary market is Southeast Asia — particularly Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam where the broker offers local bank transfer deposit methods and regional language support. The heavy marketing in these regions is what triggered the FCA and Danish FSA warnings, as the Seychelles entity was found to be soliciting clients in jurisdictions where it lacks authorisation. If you are a UK resident, the FCA warning applies directly to you — do not open an account. If you are in a market where PU Prime actively operates (SEA, Middle East, Africa), verify your entity assignment in the client agreement and understand that SD050 carries no investor protection.

sections.heading: PU Prime Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
PU Prime runs a four-tier account structure with a dramatic cost difference between the entry-level and premium tiers. The Standard and Cent accounts offer spreads from 1.3 pips on EUR/USD with zero commission — translating to an all-in cost of $13.00 per standard lot round-turn. That is expensive by 2026 standards. IC Markets Standard delivers $8.00. Exness Standard delivers approximately $10.00. PU Prime Standard is paying a 30-60% premium for the same execution.

The Prime account improves significantly: spreads from 0.0 pips plus $7.00 round-turn commission ($3.50 per side). That puts your all-in cost at approximately $7.00 per lot — competitive with most ECN offerings. But it requires a $1,000 minimum deposit.

The ECN account is where PU Prime genuinely shines: 0.0 pips plus $2.00 round-turn commission ($1.00 per side). An all-in cost of $2.00 per lot is cheaper than virtually every retail broker on the market. The catch: $10,000 minimum deposit. That locks out 95% of retail traders.

No inactivity fee (broker-stated). No deposit fee. No withdrawal fee (broker-stated). Swap rates apply to overnight positions unless you hold an Islamic account. The bonus promotions (100% deposit bonus) are aggressive — always read the withdrawal conditions attached to bonus funds.

table.footnote: All spread figures are broker-stated minimums. Real-world average spreads on Standard accounts typically range 1.3-1.8 pips EUR/USD during London/NY sessions based on publicly available comparison data. ECN averages approximately 0.1-0.3 pips.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of PU Prime?
sections.body:
Deposits are instant via card and e-wallet — standard for the industry. PU Prime's regional strength shows in its payment method diversity: local bank transfers are available for Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, and Indonesia, which means faster deposits and familiar banking for Southeast Asian traders. Crypto deposits (USDT, BTC) process within an hour for network confirmation.

Withdrawals follow a KYC-verified process. The broker states no withdrawal fees are charged. Processing times are stated as 1-3 business days for bank transfers and within 24 hours for e-wallets. Independent reports suggest most standard withdrawals process without incident — particularly for amounts under $5,000.

The complaints that exist tend to cluster around larger withdrawal amounts. Some users report delays, additional verification requests, or temporary holds when withdrawing amounts significantly larger than their deposit history. This pattern is not unique to PU Prime — it appears across many offshore brokers — but it warrants awareness if you plan to withdraw five-figure sums.

Always withdraw via the same method you deposited with. If your deposit was via Visa, your first withdrawal must return to that same Visa card up to the deposited amount. Profits above the deposit amount can be withdrawn via bank transfer or e-wallet.

table.footnote: Processing times are broker-stated. Independent reports suggest e-wallet withdrawals under $5,000 generally process within hours. Larger bank transfer withdrawals may experience additional verification delays.

sections.heading: PU Prime Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Trustpilot shows PU Prime with a 4.5/5 rating from over 1,000 reviews as of mid-2025 — a strong signal that the majority of traders who bother to leave feedback have had a generally positive experience. This is materially better than many offshore brokers which struggle to maintain above 3.5.

The withdrawal experience appears to split along two lines. For standard amounts (under $5,000) via e-wallets and crypto, processing is reported as generally fast — within 24 hours in most cases. The broker's KYC process is front-loaded, meaning once verified, subsequent withdrawals should not require additional documentation.

For larger amounts, the picture becomes less consistent. Some users report smooth withdrawals of five-figure sums. Others report delays, requests for additional source-of-funds documentation, or extended processing times. This pattern is common among brokers with offshore primary entities — the lack of external regulatory oversight means there is no mandated timeline the broker must meet.

If your withdrawal stalls: first, ensure your KYC is fully verified and your withdrawal method matches your deposit method. Second, contact support via live chat and request a specific timeline with a reference number. Third, if the broker does not resolve within their stated timeframe, escalate to the relevant regulator — ASIC if you are on the Australian entity (which has enforcement power), or the FSA Seychelles if you are offshore (which has limited enforcement capability).

NAFT has not independently tested PU Prime withdrawals. Submit your withdrawal proof at naft.com/withdrawal-proofs to help other traders.

sections.heading: How to Open a PU Prime Account — Step by Step
sections.body: The onboarding process is straightforward and optimised for speed — PU Prime targets markets where fast account opening is a competitive advantage. Available via web or the PU Prime mobile app.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit puprime.com and sign up with your email or phone number. Select your preferred account type (Cent, Standard, Prime, or ECN). You will be assigned to an entity based on your country of residence — check which entity appears in your client agreement immediately. If it says Pacific Union (Seychelles) Limited, you are on the offshore entity.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload a government-issued ID (passport or national ID) and proof of address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months). PU Prime states verification is typically completed within 24 hours. Some users report same-day approval for standard documentation.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit the $50 minimum via your preferred method. If you are in Southeast Asia, local bank transfer is fastest. Place one trade. Then immediately request a withdrawal of any amount. Time it. If the money reaches your bank or e-wallet within the stated timeframe, you know the pipeline works for your specific method and region. Only then consider scaling your deposit. Do not accept the deposit bonus until you have read the full terms and withdrawal conditions.

sections.practical_note: Deposit the minimum $50. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly within the stated timeframe, scale with confidence. If it does not — you have lost $50, not $10,000. Never accept a deposit bonus without reading the attached trading volume requirements.

sections.heading: PU Prime Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores PU Prime 6.05 out of 10 — an average trust score that reflects a broker with genuine strengths undermined by a concerning regulatory warning history. The ASIC licence is legitimate (410681). The ECN pricing ($2 all-in per lot) is genuinely competitive. The instrument range (1,000+ CFDs) is above average. And Trustpilot sentiment (4.5/5) suggests most traders have a workable experience.

But the warnings are real. The UK FCA, Danish FSA, Saskatchewan FCAA, and FinTelegram have all independently flagged this broker or its primary offshore entity. Those are not speculation — they are documented regulatory actions from four different jurisdictions. The fact that they all target the Seychelles entity (not the ASIC entity) is important context, but it does not change the reality that most of PU Prime's global clients are on that warned entity.

If you are Australian, PU Prime under ASIC is a viable option with standard protections. If you can access the ECN tier with $10,000 and understand you are on an offshore entity, the pricing is attractive. But if you are choosing between PU Prime Standard ($13 per lot, offshore entity, FCA warning) and IC Markets Raw Spread ($7 per lot, ASIC + CySEC, no warnings) — the decision makes itself.

Trade small on the offshore entity. Withdraw often. Never hold more than you can afford to lose with a broker whose primary entity has been warned by four regulators. And never accept a bonus without reading every line of the conditions.

faq.q: Is PU Prime a legit broker or a scam?
faq.a: PU Prime holds a legitimate ASIC licence (410681) in Australia, which makes it a regulated broker under Tier-1 oversight for Australian residents. But most global clients are not on the ASIC entity. They are on Pacific Union (Seychelles) Limited under FSA licence SD050 — the same entity the UK FCA has warned against for operating without authorisation. PU Prime is legit in Australia. The offshore entity has accumulated warnings from four separate regulators. That is not a scam verdict — but it is a significant compliance concern.

faq.q: How long does PU Prime withdrawal take?
faq.a: PU Prime states withdrawals process within 1-3 business days for bank transfers and within 24 hours for e-wallets. Independent reports suggest e-wallet withdrawals under $5,000 generally process within hours. Larger bank transfer withdrawals may experience additional verification delays. Some user complaints exist about difficulties withdrawing larger amounts, though Trustpilot sentiment (4.5/5) suggests most traders have a functional withdrawal experience.

faq.q: Is PU Prime regulated by the FCA?
faq.a: No. PU Prime does not hold an FCA licence and does not claim FCA regulation. The UK FCA has issued a specific warning against Pacific Union (Seychelles) Limited — the entity that serves most of PU Prime's global clients — for operating without FCA authorisation. This means PU Prime was soliciting UK clients without being registered to do so. UK residents should not open accounts with PU Prime.

faq.q: What is the PU Prime minimum deposit in 2026?
faq.a: PU Prime minimum deposit is $50 for Cent and Standard accounts, $1,000 for the Prime account, and $10,000 for the ECN account. The competitive ECN pricing ($2 all-in per lot) is only accessible at the $10,000 tier. Standard account traders pay $13 per lot all-in, which is expensive relative to competitors like IC Markets or Exness.

faq.q: Why did the FCA warn against PU Prime?
faq.a: The FCA warning (updated January 2026) is against Pacific Union (Seychelles) Limited for operating without FCA authorisation in the UK. This means the Seychelles entity was soliciting UK-based clients without being registered with the FCA. PU Prime does not claim FCA regulation — the warning is for operating without it. This does not affect the ASIC licence (which remains active) but it signals aggressive cross-border marketing by the offshore entity.

faq.q: Is PU Prime safe for traders in Malaysia and Indonesia?
faq.a: Malaysian and Indonesian traders are routed to the Seychelles offshore entity (FSA licence SD050) with no investor compensation scheme. PU Prime offers local bank transfer deposits and regional language support in these markets, which explains its popularity. However, neither Malaysia nor Indonesia formally regulates PU Prime — there is no local licence. You are trading on an offshore entity with 1:1000 leverage and no safety net. Keep balances manageable and withdraw profits regularly.

faq.q: What is the difference between PU Prime and Pacific Union CySEC?
faq.a: Pacific Union Group Ltd (CySEC-regulated) has explicitly stated it is NOT part of the PU Prime scheme. Kraken acquired this CySEC entity separately and renamed it Greenfields Wealth. PU Prime does not hold and has never held a CySEC licence. If you see references to PU Prime having CySEC regulation, that information is incorrect. The two brands share a historical name connection but are operationally and legally separate.

faq.q: What leverage does PU Prime offer?
faq.a: Leverage depends on which entity holds your account. ASIC entity (Australian residents): 1:30 on majors — standard Australian retail caps. Offshore Seychelles entity (most global clients): up to 1:1000. The headline 1:1000 leverage only applies to the offshore entity with zero investor protection. At 1:1000, a 0.1% adverse move wipes your entire margin. This is not a feature for retail traders — it is a mechanism that accelerates account liquidation.
